> I want to build a mixer for my PC with four faders, mute buttons and 6.35‑mm audio jacks. I have taken apart a faulty mixer and photographed its boards so that I can spot parts that I might reuse. Those parts still need to be tested. I plan to design the circuit in KiCad and to make a 3D‑printed enclosure.

### 2026-10-21 – I started ReMix by taking apart an AMPRO mixer that wasn't working anymore. I looked at the four-channel board. Took pictures of both sides. I checked the faders the buttons, the LEDs, the rotary cont

**5h**

I started ReMix by taking apart an AMPRO mixer that wasn't working anymore. I looked at the four-channel board. Took pictures of both sides. I checked the faders the buttons, the LEDs, the rotary controls, the XLR sockets and the 6.35 mm jacks to see which parts I could use again. I saw the markings PM4CH-A and PM4CH-B on the board. I still don't know the values of the faders. The parts need to be tested. My next step is to use a multimeter to check the faders before I start making the circuit and the new case.

Usa "four sessions of five hours each" solo se corrisponde alle ore realmente lavorate. Ecco il testo in inglese, oltre 200 parole:

Across four sessions of five hours each I worked on the development of ReMix, a DIY desktop mixer for my PC. My goal is to combine audio controls with the ability to adjust application volumes using recovered components and a custom 3D-printed enclosure. I started by disassembling a faulty AMPRO mixer and documenting its circuit boards with photographs. I inspected the faders, rotary controls, buttons, LEDs and audio connectors to identify reusable parts. The original mixer had suffered capacitor failures so I kept the extracted board disconnected from power during the checks. I tested one pair of terminals on each of the four faders using a multimeter. On the fader I measured approximately 16.6 ohms at one end 14.33 kilohms halfway through its travel and 19.7 kilohms at the opposite end. The resistance changed smoothly without jumps and the other faders produced similar results. Since these measurements were taken with the components still soldered to the board they do not confirm the pinout, resistance curve or nominal value. I also measured the fader bodies and their travel to support the enclosure design. With AI assistance I prepared an enclosure concept, a DXF panel drawing, a parametric 3D model, preliminary STL files and visual previews. This is still a draft, than a finished working mixer. The next steps are to confirm the audio requirements and fader connections develop the KiCad circuit and complete the component mounts and connector openings before building and testing a prototype.
